skill.name: binary-re-synthesis
skill.description: Compiles binary reverse engineering findings into evidence-based reports with validated hypotheses, capability maps, and recommendations.
skill.summary: Turn binary analysis evidence into structured, traceable reverse engineering reports.
skill.author: 2389-research

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives. The skill is a markdown-based reporting guide for binary reverse engineering and does not contain executable commands, live network activity, weak cryptography, log deletion, or prompt injection evidence.

remediation.issue: Static scanners may misread fenced report examples as executable commands.
remediation.suggestion: Label example blocks as text or markdown where possible, and avoid language markers that imply runnable shell or Ruby code.

remediation.issue: Example indicators include an internal IP address and log path that can look like active behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that network destinations, file paths, and security findings are illustrative evidence from analyzed binaries.

content.value_statement: Binary analysis often produces scattered facts that are hard to share. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code turn evidence into clear reports with confidence levels and next steps.
actual_capabilities: Reviews facts from triage, static analysis, and dynamic analysis phases.
Classifies hypotheses as confirmed, refuted, uncertain, or unvalidated.
Maps observed binary capabilities across network, file system, and cryptography areas.
Generates structured markdown reports with evidence logs and recommendations.
Creates final knowledge journal entries for completed binary analysis sessions.
Formats findings for human readers, databases, or threat intelligence workflows.
limitations: Requires prior analysis facts; it does not perform triage, disassembly, or dynamic testing by itself.
Report quality depends on the accuracy and completeness of supplied evidence.
Cannot prove behavior that was not observed or supported by prior findings.
Threat intelligence formats still need analyst review before external sharing.

use_cases.title: Prepare a handoff report
use_cases.description: Summarize reverse engineering results for another analyst or incident response team.

use_cases.title: Validate malware hypotheses
use_cases.description: Compare evidence from static and dynamic analysis before declaring binary behavior.

use_cases.title: Archive completed research
use_cases.description: Create a durable record of conclusions, evidence, unknowns, and recommended follow-up work.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize my findings
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner report creation after collecting notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the binary-re-synthesis skill to summarize my current binary analysis notes into an executive summary, confirmed capabilities, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Validate hypotheses against evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the binary-re-synthesis skill to review each hypothesis, mark it confirmed, refuted, uncertain, or unvalidated, and cite the supporting evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Create a stakeholder report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced reporting for incident response or management.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the binary-re-synthesis skill to produce a stakeholder-ready report with artifact details, behavioral summary, evidence log, risk findings, and recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare threat intelligence output
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the binary-re-synthesis skill to convert confirmed malicious behavior into threat intelligence language, including capabilities, confidence, evidence, and remaining unknowns.

output_examples.input: Notes include a network function, TLS imports, a telemetry string, and one observed outbound connection.
output_examples.output: A concise report states that the binary is likely a telemetry client, explains the confidence level, lists supporting evidence, and recommends payload review.

output_examples.input: The analyst has three hypotheses, with mixed evidence for persistence and strong evidence for configuration parsing.
output_examples.output: A hypothesis table separates confirmed, refuted, and uncertain claims, then lists the exact evidence needed to close remaining gaps.

output_examples.input: A completed malware analysis needs archival documentation for future investigations.
output_examples.output: A final journal entry records the artifact identity, confirmed capabilities, security findings, unresolved questions, and evidence index.

best_practices: Run this skill after collecting evidence from triage, static analysis, and dynamic analysis.
Keep every conclusion tied to a specific observation, function, string, trace, or tool result.
Separate confirmed behavior from speculation and unresolved questions.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to invent findings when evidence is missing.
Do not present potential capabilities as confirmed behavior.
Do not share threat intelligence output externally without human review.

faq.question: Does this skill analyze binaries directly?
faq.answer: No. It synthesizes evidence that was already collected by triage, static analysis, and dynamic analysis work.

faq.question: Can it produce reports for malware analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize malware analysis findings, evidence, confidence levels, and recommended follow-up actions.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Provide artifact metadata, hypotheses, function notes, strings, dynamic observations, tool outputs, and unresolved questions.

faq.question: Does it support non-malicious firmware or application binaries?
faq.answer: Yes. The templates cover general binary capabilities, file access, network behavior, configuration parsing, and reporting.

faq.question: How does it handle uncertainty?
faq.answer: It labels hypotheses as confirmed, refuted, uncertain, or unvalidated, and asks for more evidence where needed.

faq.question: Can it create machine-readable summaries?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes structured output options for tools, databases, and threat intelligence workflows.
